<security_assessment>

<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It lists standard package information such as name, version, source URL, dependencies, and checksums. The source is fetched from the official GitHub repository of the project (https://github.com/netromdk/vermin), which matches the declared upstream URL. The source archive is pinned to a specific tag (v1.9.1), ensuring reproducibility. The md5sum is provided and matches the expected value for the release tarball, which helps verify integrity.

There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, unexpected network locations, or suspicious commands. The dependencies listed are typical for Python packages built using modern Python packaging tools (setuptools, build, installer, wheel). The `noextract` directive is used correctly for a source that will be handled by the corresponding PKGBUILD, which is standard practice. No executable code or scripts are present in this file, and it does not perform any actions on its own.

This file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and shows no evidence of malicious intent or supply chain compromise.
</details>
